```{r}
#shortcut for installing necessary packages.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning=FALSE, message = FALSE)

packages <- c("tidygeocoder", "sf", "terra", "tidyverse", "tidycensus", "flextable", "tmap")
installed <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(!installed)) {install.packages(packages[!installed])}

```

##Geocoding

#Q1. Import this In N Out Burger CSV file.

```{r q1chunk1}
#part a.
download.file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pjames-ucdavis/SPH215/refs/heads/main/innout_final.csv","innout_final.csv", mode = "wb")

#part b.
in_n_out <- read_csv("innout_final.csv")
```

#Q2. Glimpse at the data. What is the address field that you might want to geocode?
```         
We would want to geocode the "store address" field. 
```
```{r q2chunk2}
#Glimpse at data. 
glimpse(in_n_out)

#To view data as an Excel document. 
view(in_n_out)

#Look specifically at "store address" column.
head(in_n_out$`store address`)

```
#Q3. Geocode the data using the “arcgis” geocoder in the tidygeocoder package.
```{r q3chunk3}
in_n_out_geo <- geocode(in_n_out,"store address", method = "arcgis")
head(in_n_out_geo)
```

#Q4. Take a look at the lat and long columns. Do we have missing data?
     Based on the summary reports, there are no missing (NAs) addresses for the 
     latitude or the longitude.
```{r q4chunk4}
#check for missing data in each column 

#latitude
summary(in_n_out_geo$lat)

#longitude
summary(in_n_out_geo$long)

```

#Q5.Make the data set spatial with a CRS of WGS 84 (hint: crs=4326).
```{r q5chunk5}
#Specify the lat, long coordinates for R
in_n_out_points <- st_as_sf(in_n_out_geo, coords = c("long", "lat"))

#check if there's a CRS.
st_crs(in_n_out_points)           #ResultCRS:NA

#Set CRS of WGS 84
in_n_out_crs <- st_set_crs(in_n_out_points, 4326)

#Check the CRS
st_crs(in_n_out_crs)

```

#Q6. Map the addresses using the tmap package. Make the points red.
```{r q6chunk6}

#Establish Map View 
tmap_mode("view")

#Map w/ Red Points
burger_map = tm_shape(in_n_out_crs) + tm_dots( fill = "red", size= 0.3, fill_alpha = 0.5)
burger_map

```

#Q7. Make blue points!
```{r q7chunk7}

#Establish Map View 
tmap_mode("view")

#Map w/ Blue Points
burger_map_b = tm_shape(in_n_out_crs) + tm_dots( fill = "blue", size= 0.3, fill_alpha = 0.5)
burger_map_b

```

##Map Point Health Data

#Q8. Import the CAdata dataset from the MapGAM package.
The MapGAM package wouldn't load, so I imported the data from the class GitHUb.
```{r q8chunk8}

#CAdata Dataset
download.file("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pjames-ucdavis/SPH215/refs/heads/main/CAdata.rds", "CAdata.rds", mode = "wb")

#read CAdata
cancer <- readRDS("CAdata.rds")

#View dataset 
summary(cancer)
view (cancer)

```

#Q9. Add a coordinate reference system to the CAdata dataset and make sure it’s a spatial dataset that you can map.
```{r q9chunk9}
#Define the "X" and "Y" coordinates for R. 
cancer_points <- st_as_sf(cancer, coords=c("X","Y"))

#Identify if there's a CRS.
st_crs(cancer_points)          #CRSResult: NA

#Load CRS dataset
ca_projection <- "+proj=lcc +lat_1=40 +lat_2=41.66666666666666 
             +lat_0=39.33333333333334 +lon_0=-122 +x_0=2000000 
             +y_0=500000.0000000002 +ellps=GRS80 
             +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs"
#Add CRS
cancer_points_crs <- st_set_crs(cancer_points, ca_projection)

#Check CRS
st_crs(cancer_points_crs)

#Confirmed it's a spatial data set!
```

#Q10. Create a map of the CAdata data set with points color coded by Insurance Status using the tmap package.
```{r q10chunk10}

#Establish Map Interactive Mode 
tmap_mode("view")

#Construct a map based on "Insurance Status in CA"
insur_map = tm_shape(cancer_points_crs) + tm_dots(fill="INS", fill.scale=tm_scale_categorical())

#View Map
insur_map

```

##Census Data

#Q11. Use the tidycensus package to download American Community Survey Five year estimates from 2018-2022 in California at the Census tract level for the following variable: a. Household Median Income = “B19013_001”
```{r q11chunk11}
#census_api_key("86fccf503d859dae6884ddca2dbf66c8372bc5c7", install = TRUE)"
#API Key saved to R Environment - comment out to avoid multiple downloads 

#Loading variable in ACS data set from 2018-2022   
acs2022 <- load_variables(2022, "acs5", cache = TRUE)
view(acs2022)

#Extract Household Median Income data from 2018-2022
ca <- get_acs(geography = "tract", 
              year = 2022,
              variables = c(medincome = "B19013_001"), 
              state = "CA",
              survey = "acs5",
              output = "wide")
ca

```

#Q12. Take a glimpse at your data
```{r q12chunk12}

glimpse(ca)

```

#Q13. Give us the mean median household income across tracts in California.
```{r q13chunk13}
#Descriptive statistics Include na.rm = TRUE argument to omit "missingness". 

ca %>%
summarize(Mean = mean(medincomeE, na.rm = TRUE))

#The mean median household income across tracts in CA is $99,732.02.
```

#Q14. Make a table showing the mean, median, and standard deviation of median household income across tract in California, and make it look fancy!
```{r q14chunk14}
#The mean, median, and SD of median household incomes acorss tract in CA
tract <- ca %>%
summarize (Mean = mean(medincomeE, na.rm = TRUE),
   Median = median(medincomeE, na.rm = TRUE),
   SD = sd(medincomeE, na.rm = TRUE))

#Table summary of Measure of Central Tendency 
ttable  <- flextable (tract)
ttable

#Table w/ clearer labels 
tract_table <- ttable %>% 
  set_header_labels(Mean ="Mean", Median = "Median", SD = "Standard Deviation") %>% flextable::align(align = "center", part = "all")

tract_table

```

#Q15. Create a histogram of median household income across tracts in California. 
Make sure it has a label.
```{r q15chunk15}

#create histogram across tracts in CA  
ca %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x=medincomeE)) + xlab("CA Median Household Income")

```

#Q16. OK now give me a boxplot! And I want a nice label for this too.
```{r q16chunk16}
#create boxplot for MHI across CA tract
ca %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(y = medincomeE,)) + ylab("CA Median Household Income")

```
